item.title: IndyCar Gave Palou a Home Race and Took Newgarden’s. Don’t Call It Neutral
item.description: Josef Newgarden’s No. 2 carried Astemo branding in 2026. Photo: Team Penske Count the Sundays. In 2026, IndyCar’s third Sunday of July belonged to Nashville Superspeedway. In 2027, it belongs to the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, where the inaugural INDYCAR Grand Prix of Barcelona is set for July 18. Nobody involved has said one replaced the other. The calendar, unfortunately, doesn’t need anyone’s permission to look suggestive. What’s confirmed, and what isn’t IndyCar released Phase Two of its 2027 schedule on October 23, completing a 17-race season that FOX will carry from start to finish. Nashville isn’t on it. Neither is the Freedom 250 Grand Prix that ran through Washington, D.C., in August. The Borchetta Bourbon Music City Grand Prix’s own website says the 2027 schedule is “now confirmed without an event in Nashville,” thanks the fans, and credits partners from downtown Nashville to the Superspeedway. What it doesn’t offer is a reason, a contract status, or a road back. Everything past that is paddock chatter, and chatter stays out of this story. The D.C. absence is the easier one to read. IndyCar tied that race to the 250th anniversary of American independence, Kyle Kirkwood won it ( we covered how ), and the series reported 3,282,000 viewers for the broadcast. It simply isn’t on next year’s list. Barcelona is the only new event IndyCar named in the Phase Two release. Barcelona didn’t start as a vacancy notice By Mark Miles’ own account, the Barcelona deal began with a call from the circuit , not the other way around, and turned into roughly four months of talks. It’s a multiyear agreement that Miles suggested could run about a decade, and it makes Barcelona the series’ first race outside North America since São Paulo in 2013 and its first in Europe since Assen in 2007. He also floated the track as a possible home base for IndyCar in Europe. That isn’t how anyone describes a stopgap for a missing oval. Do the arithmetic, though. Four months before an October 23 announcement lands in late June, weeks before Nashville Superspeedway hosted its 2026 race. That’s a timeline, not an allegation. It does mean Spain was a live conversation while Nashville was still an upcoming date on the 2026 calendar. For what the Catalunya circuit demands of tires and weather forecasts, Michelin’s view from the WEC weekend is worth a read. The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya main grandstand, where IndyCar is scheduled to race on July 18, 2027. Josef Newgarden, a Nashville native, won the 2025 race at the Superspeedway by 0.5021 seconds over Alex Palou. It was his first win of that season, it ended a 20-race drought, and it was his first at home. In 2026 the script flipped: Palou led the final 95 of 225 laps and beat Newgarden by 0.8731 seconds for his first Nashville win. item.title: Hellebuyck Returns Ready To Play For New Jersey Against Dallas
item.description: Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images Connor Hellebuyck is not waiting for permission to start playing again. The veteran goaltender told reporters on Monday that he feels ready to go right now, even though he has not played a game this season. His first appearance in New Jersey comes Tuesday night versus the Dallas Stars, occurring merely four days after a trade from Winnipeg concluded a months-long standoff. Training Hard While Sitting Out Many athletes let their skills fade when they are stuck on the sidelines, but Hellebuyck did not take that route. ESPN reports that he practiced five to six days weekly in Michigan while suspended. Robby Fabbri and Antonio Stranges, both free agent forwards, trained with him, and he approached these sessions with the same intensity as a full NHL camp. He noted that the goalposts were not drilled into the ice like they are for real games, and both forwards shot left-handed, which limited his practice options. Yet he kept working. He said, “If you’re asking me, I’m ready today,” Hellebuyck said Monday. “But I don’t make every decision around here.” The trade that brought him to New Jersey cost the Devils a significant package. The team sent forward Dawson Mercer, goaltender Nico Daws, prospect Alexander Command, and two draft picks to Winnipeg. This move marks the biggest play yet for first-year general manager Sunny Mehta. Mehta was hired this summer after working with the Florida Panthers. The Devils currently sit at 7-4-0 and are riding a three-game win streak into this road trip. Getting Used to the Traffic Again After spending 11 years with the Winnipeg Jets, Hellebuyck knows the league well, but he still has work to do on his timing. Winnipeg signed him in 2023 to a seven-year contract, and he is currently in the third year of that deal. During that time, he forfeited more than $900,000 in salary because he did not report to training camp. Now he must relearn how to handle screens and rebounds in a new system. “The important part is seeing some screens and reacting to some rebounds, and getting a feel for some righties,” said Hellebuyck. His last start came on April 13 against the Vegas Golden Knights, where he allowed six goals on 38 shots. The Dallas Stars head into Tuesday after winning their last five games. Hellebuyck has a mixed history against Dallas, holding a 14-12-6 record in 32 career meetings. However, his last seven matchups with the Stars have been rough, with just one win and a 3.20 goals-against average. Despite these stats, the mood is positive. “I’m just really excited to play hockey again,” Hellebuyck said. “That was the hardest part about all of this, wanting to go back and not being able to.” A Fresh Start for the Devils New Jersey has only one other goalie on the roster, veteran Jake Allen. This means Hellebuyck’s arrival immediately changes the team’s dynamic. The three-time Vezina Trophy winner and Olympic gold medalist brings a proven track record to a young squad. item.title: Spurs bring designer streetwear, cowboy flair to Frost Bank Center ahead of Kings game
item.description: Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper arrive together at Frost Bank Center ahead of Tuesday's game against the Sacramento Kings. (Courtesy of San Antonio Spurs) The San Antonio Spurs brought a mix of luxury streetwear, bold graphics and Texas cowboy flair to Frost Bank Center on Tuesday ahead of their matchup against the Sacramento Kings. Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Devin Vassell and Keldon Johnson showed off their personal styles as they arrived at the arena. Designer labels including Balenciaga, Chrome Hearts, Carhartt WIP and ERCOLE STUDIO made appearances. The Slash Bros arrived together, with the young Spurs teammates sporting contrasting streetwear looks. Castle made a statement in a bright red Balenciaga hoodie featuring the fashion house's logo across the chest. He paired it with Balenciaga VIC Skater Graffiti sweatpants, which had an oversized fit and black-and-white, graffiti-inspired graphics. He completed the look with a black-and-white Chrome Hearts Skully Cross Logo beanie and a black backpack. Harper kept things simple alongside Castle, wearing a black Nike Kobe Bryant hoodie with a small gold Mamba logo on the chest. The Spurs rookie completed his laid-back look with black pants and white sneakers. Vassell opted for a graphic-heavy streetwear look, wearing an ERCOLE STUDIO gray graphic-print raw-edge T-shirt. The blue-gray shirt featured a woman's face and a lighthouse, with "Holy Water" printed across the front. He paired it with loose-fitting black pants and gray sneakers and carried blue over-ear headphones. Johnson, meanwhile, brought a little Texas swagger to the arena in a black cowboy hat and a red, black and white Carhartt WIP plaid patch-pocket shirt layered over a black T-shirt. He paired the Western-inspired outfit with black pants and a silver cross necklace. His mustache added another touch of cowboy flair. From Castle and Harper's coordinated arrival to Johnson's Western-inspired outfit, the Spurs continued to showcase their individual personalities through their game-day fashion. San Antonio hosts Sacramento on Tuesday night at Frost Bank Center. Tipoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Matt LaFleur cuts refs some slack despite screwing Packers over in Lions game
item.description: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Matt LaFleur cuts refs some slack despite screwing Packers over in Lions game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers fell to a 4-3 record after suffering a tough 20-17 Week 7 loss to the Detroit Lions. Although many believe the club got a bit screwed over by some controversial officiating, head coach Matt LaFleur took it easy on NFL referees on Tuesday. When the questionable officiating was brought up to the 46-year-old again, LaFleur seemingly took the high road. He admitted that referees have a difficult job , as they have to make decisions based on plays that happen in an instant, according to Ryan Wood of USA Today Sports. LaFleur ended his statement claiming that all he wants to see as a coach is consistent officiating. “I don’t think officiating in this league is very easy,” LaFleur said. “I really don’t. I think things happen quickly, and there’s some bang-bang decisions they have to make. So I don’t think they have an easy job. All you want as a coach is consistency.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Green Bay was given controversial penalties late in the second half that helped the Lions secure the win. A roughing-the-passer call in the third quarter on Packers defensive end Brenton Cox even had future Hall of Fame quarterback turned announcer Tom Brady up in arms . There were also penalties called on defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt, defensive tackle Karl Brooks, and quarterback Jordan Love that left viewers scratching their heads. NFL coaches and players are not typically allowed to ridicule officials, as it can result in heavy fines or suspensions. That rule may play a part in Matt LaFleur’s comments on Tuesday. Either way, the Packers will move on to Week 8 for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Carolina Panthers. item.title: Not knowing the rules or practicing penalties: How Fleetwood knocked out Arsenal in Carabao Cup’s greatest shock
item.description: In the delirium of Fleetwood Town ’s victory over Premier League champions Arsenal , in perhaps the biggest shock in Carabao Cup history, there were no secrets, no hidden tactics. Instead, manager Matt Lawlor celebrated the greatest win of his career and the most momentous night in Fleetwood’s history with disarming honesty. “We haven't practised once,” he said, after the League Two side converted five of the coolest penalties you are ever going to see, right up to 19-year-old centre-back Conor Haughey putting their final one top bins. “I'm not going to blag that we had some meticulous penalties [planned], we haven't.” Lawlor hadn’t been too sure of the rules, either. As Fleetwood were hanging on against Arsenal’s second-half siege and substitute Martin Odegaard threatened to crack the code that was their deep defence with a moment of magic, Lawlor thought his team were clinging on for extra-time until one of his assistants reminded him the English Football League scrapped that years ago. “I thought, ‘Oh my lord, thank God for that’”, he grinned. Fleetwood, positioned 84 places below Arsenal, knocked the champions out on penalties (Getty) But there was commitment, heart and discipline aplenty at (their) Highbury. Fleetwood had lost five of their last seven matches since they knocked out Sheffield United in the third round last month and drew the champions, as if booking the biggest night in the club’s history on the Fylde Coast had distracted them away from an unbeaten start. Lawlor looked at his young squad and accepted they would go through dips of form, but backed them to come good again on the big occasion. Arsenal had not conceded in the Premier League in three games but they were breached after just 21 minutes to a side that were 18th in League Two and 84 places below them. There was a ruthlessness about the manner the on-loan Fulham forward Aaron Loupalo-Bi targeted the 17-year-old Arsenal centre-back Marli Salmon, one of three teenagers in the visiting line-up, shrugging him aside before finishing past debutant goalkeeper Illan Meslier. But Fleetwood had to pick at the gaps. Arteta made nine changes from Saturday’s 2-0 win over Everton but still fielded two forwards in Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz who cost a combined £100m. Martin Zubimendi played in the World Cup final three months ago. Arsenal had Odegaard, Eberechi Eze and Bruno Guimaraes in reserve and all three needed to be chucked on. It was only the introduction of Odegaard, though, that created doubt and danger. And the champions were repelled magnificently. Rhys Bennett, somehow, was in the right place to block a Havertz volley from point-blank after Gyokeres had pulled one back. Jay Lynch, the goalkeeper, lost his voice directing his back-line from side to side. item.title: George Russell F1 title chances defended by Toto Wolff after Helmut Marko comments
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes Formula 1 team chief Toto Wolff has rejected former Red Bull motorsport adviser Helmut Marko's claim that George Russell will never get another shot at the F1 title. Russell currently sits 123 points behind his team-mate and current championship leader Kimi Antonelli in the drivers' standings. While speaking to Sky Sports Deutschland ahead of the United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas, Marko said Antonelli had taken over as the Brackley outfit's lead driver. "Russell is no longer the number one driver. Antonelli has quite clearly taken that spot from him. But Russell is one of the top drivers," Marko said. "I doubt whether he’ll ever have another chance at the world title or be given number one status anywhere." Asked about the comments after the race in Austin, Wolff said Marko had got it wrong. Helmut Marko, Red Bull Racing Helmut Marko, Red Bull Racing "I start with Helmut, I mean, he’s my Austrian, not-so-buddy, but I respect his opinion. But I think he’s wrong on George. George has all the ability. I think the car doesn’t suit him." He added: "I think that at the beginning of the season, it is maybe difficult to cope with the situation where you’re feeling that this is my year to come, and then we have this wonderkid on the other side that starts to really chip away. And I believe that a new season, George, if we provide him with a quick car, is absolutely possible. "He has absolutely what it needs to win a championship. So I think it's a bit too easy to say, let's forget about all these years where he won in F2 and F3, his rookie years and the European championships back-to-back in karting, that's still all there." item.title: McKeel's Swinburne back on track as he wins twice at district swim meet
item.description: WAUCHULA — It hasn’t exactly been a senior season that McKeel’s Chance Swinburne expected. “I've been sick for most of the season, so it kind of took it away from me of wanting to continue,” he said. Yet as the season winds down and he’s begun to feel better, he's starting to feel better about competing. Although he said he's not going to swim competitively after high school, he’s hoping to cap his career with his best performances at the state meet. The road to state began on Tuesday, Oct. 27 as he had little trouble winning his two individual events to help lead the McKeel boys to runner-up finish behind host Hardee in the Class 2A, District 7 Swimming and Diving Meet at the Hardee Recreational Complex. 4A-7 district swimming: Jenkins' Nico Lee wins 100 fly, sets PR in 100 breast at 4A-7 meet County swim meet: Cabrera sets county mark, McKeel sweeps team titles Ridge meet: Winter Haven sweeps boys, girls win titles at rain-shortened Ridge meet Breakout season: McKeel's Claire Scarborough emerges swimmer to beat in Polk For the girls, Bryce Palmer and Claire Swinburne each won two individual events, and Elin Jonsson and Jocelyn Chanthavongsa each won one individual event to help lead the girls to the team district title. As the only individual winner for the boys, Swinburne won the 200-yard freestyle in 1:50.83, then later won the 100 freestyle in 49.14. He was the only swimmer to go sub-50 in the event. Swinburne said he was happy with his times as he wasn’t pushing for fast times. In each race, Swinburne had a slight lead in the first half of the race before pulling away for decisive wins. “I’m not trying to go for anything here,” he said. “I already know I'm making regionals. I’ve had a weird practice schedule, but it's not really swimming. Like last week, Friday and Saturday, they (club) have practices, so I've been to this meet with one day. I'm not expecting much of it.” Swinburne changed clubs in the past year and now goes to Winter Garden for club practice. “I’ve been training with all these people, and I don't get to race them at all,” he said. “There are not a lot of people that I can compete with (during the season). Hardee is kind of like the only (team) that I can find someone to compete against, because Marcos Cabrera and I don't swim the same events.” McKeel coach Roy Wilshire said he has seen some improvement in Swinburne’s performance recently and said he’s in a good spot if he can stay healthy over the next couple of weeks. “He's got the right mindset,” he said. “He knows kind of where his ceiling is there with just a couple of meets left. Beasley is scheduled to enter his guilty plea in Brooklyn federal court on Dec. 9, his attorney, Steve Haney, told The Athletic . Beasley had been negotiating a plea agreement with federal prosecutors, and an overnight court docket notice indicated that he intended to plead guilty, according to ESPN . Beasley had not yet signed a plea agreement when Haney spoke with the outlet, the attorney said. The case stems from allegations that Beasley, 29, manipulated his performance during some games in the 2023-24 NBA season and that others used information about his expected statistics to place bets, according to the U.S. Department of Justice ’s June announcement of the athlete’s indictment. Beasley was indicted alongside former NBA player Edward Davis, NBA player agent Paolo Zamorano and three other men: William Brown, Robert Gorodetsky and Ernesto Plascencia, according to the Justice Department. The defendants were charged with “wire fraud conspiracy, bribery in sporting contests, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, and money laundering conspiracy for their alleged roles in a scheme to bribe Beasley to manipulate his performance in NBA games and use inside information about Beasley’s intended performance to profit via illegal betting activity,” the Justice Department said in a news release at the time. item.title: Where does Utah rank in some of Morgan Scalley’s key stats for success?
item.description: Utah head coach Morgan Scalley smiles before a game against Houston at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News Each week, Utah coach Morgan Scalley and his staff pour over film to prepare the team for the opposing team’s tendencies and to try to find any weaknesses that the Utes can exploit. While watching Houston’s film, Utah noticed that Houston allowed a lot of quarterback running lanes. Quarterback Devon Dampier was able to use that to his advantage, rushing for 150 yards and two touchdowns in the Utes’ 21-13 win over the Cougars. “We always take what the defense gives us,” Dampier said. “Just watching film, there was a lot of running lanes, quarterback lanes during dropback passes. (Coaches) just emphasized, ‘Devon, if you see it, go take it.’” The eye test and film breakdowns are king in football, but statistics and analytics have their place as well, especially as predictors of future success. Scalley has studied the best teams in college football over the past 20 years and has identified statistics that are predictive of success. Obviously, scoring offense and defense are the two most important statistics, but digging deeper, what are others that lead to wins? Rush defense, Scalley says, is a big one. While total rushing yards “doesn’t show up as a big stat” for the current top teams in the country, yards per rush is a big tell. It’s all about efficiency. “Are you rushing the ball efficiently? According to Hauler Talk , NASCAR sent a Microsoft Teams message to teams throughout pit road on Sunday, warning that drivers could be black-flagged if they failed to increase their speed during the fuel-saving parade. The message reportedly made it clear that NASCAR was no longer willing to let the field continue running at an unacceptably slow pace. And honestly, this is exactly the kind of enforcement superspeedway racing needs. For years, fuel saving has played a major role in races at tracks like Daytona and Talladega. While managing fuel has always been part of racing, there is a difference between strategy that adds another layer to the competition and a situation where drivers spend lap after lap riding around at reduced speed to stretch their fuel mileage. When the entire field is more concerned with saving fuel than racing, it becomes difficult for fans to get excited about what they are watching. The constant fuel-saving strategies can take away from the side-by-side battles, aggressive moves and unpredictable finishes that have made superspeedway racing one of NASCAR’s biggest attractions. Enforcing a rule that requires drivers to maintain a reasonable pace could be one way to change that. If NASCAR follows through on its warning and consistently black-flags drivers who refuse to pick up the pace, teams would have to reconsider how they approach these races. Instead of being able to run well below full speed for extended periods, teams would face a real consequence for prioritizing fuel mileage over maintaining the pace of the race. That doesn’t mean fuel strategy should disappear completely. Fuel mileage has always been part of motorsports, and NASCAR shouldn’t eliminate every strategic element that comes with it. However, there needs to be a balance between fuel management and putting on a competitive show. The key will be consistency. If NASCAR only threatens penalties but rarely follows through, teams will have little reason to change their approach. If officials are serious about enforcing the rule, however, it could force teams to adjust their strategies and make the racing more competitive. There are still questions about how the rule would be applied, what speed NASCAR would consider acceptable and how officials would account for legitimate fuel-saving situations.
